urban_flood.note: Spring thaw ponding and ice jams (north), then convective downpours in May-July (Shymkent, Almaty, Astana).

haze.note: Steppe and forest fires June-September (Kostanay 2022, Abai 2023) and winter coal-smoke smog in Almaty and Astana (December-January inversions).

water.note: Drought and pasture failure in summer (2021); irrigation shortfalls on the Syr Darya in July-August; falling Caspian/Ural levels are a chronic trend.

KAZ.country_note_ja: Kazakhstan's hazard profile splits sharply by region: the south-east (Almaty, Jetisu, Jambyl, Turkistan) carries almost all of the earthquake and mudflow risk (ThinkHazard High; GEM AAL USD 16 M/yr concentrated in South Kazakhstan and Almaty), while the north and west are dominated by spring snowmelt floods (2024: more than 120,000 evacuated), steppe/forest fires and extreme cold. Water scarcity is rated High nationally and the Caspian and Ural are at historic lows. Global indices rate the country low-risk overall (WorldRiskIndex 2025: 2.18, rank 155/193; INFORM 2025: 2.7, rank 135/191), mainly because exposure and vulnerability are low, not because hazards are absent.

history.name_ja: 1887 Verny (Almaty) earthquake, Mw 7.3-7.7, MSK X
history.where: Verny (Almaty), Trans-Ili Alatau foothills
history.note_ja: Destroyed the city of Verny; at least 332 killed in the city plus 154 in mountain landslides per the article body (lead says 'at least 330'). Magnitude is a macroseismic estimate; not in USGS ComCat (pre-1900).

history.name_ja: 1911 Kemin (Chon-Kemin / Kebin) earthquake, Mw 8.0
history.where: Chon-Kemin valley (Kyrgyzstan) - Almaty, epicentre 37 km from Almaty

history.name_ja: 1921 Malaya Almatinka debris flow (Almaty mudflow)
history.where: Small Almaty (Malaya Almatinka) valley - central Almaty
history.note_ja: Rain-triggered mudflow of about 10 million m3 killed about 500 of Almaty's 45,000 residents and destroyed much of the city; the reason the Medeu dam was built. Day of month from secondary knowledge (unverified); year confirmed.

history.name_ja: 1973 Medeu mudflow stopped by the new Medeu dam
history.where: Medeu valley above Almaty
history.note_ja: Glacial-lake outburst mudflow; the dam, completed just in time, captured 3.8 million m3 of sediment and saved the city. Deaths 0 is inferred from the article (none reported).

history.name_ja: 2003 Lugovoe (Zhambyl Region) earthquake
history.where: Lugovoe / Ryskulov district, Jambyl Region (location from memory)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 2003 earthquake total for Kazakhstan: 3 deaths, 36,626 affected. Location and exact date are from memory (unverified); the EM-DAT figures are page_read.

history.name_ja: 2008 spring floods in South Kazakhstan (Shymkent area)
history.where: South Kazakhstan Region (now Turkistan/Shymkent) - location from memory

history.name_ja: 2010 Kyzylagash (Qyzylaghash) dam failure flood
history.where: Kyzylagash village, Aksu district (then Almaty Region, now Jetisu)
history.note_ja: Dam burst around 22:00 on 11 March after rain and sudden snowmelt; at least 43 killed, 211 injured, over 1,000 evacuated (Wikipedia). EM-DAT 2010 flood total 44 deaths, 29,200 affected, USD 34.6 M. A second dam broke the next day in the Aksu/Karatal area (press).

history.name_ja: 2015 Kargaly moraine-lake outburst mudflow, Almaty (Nauryzbay district)
history.where: Kargalinka river - Chapaevo, Kargaly, Kamenka (Nauryzbay district, Almaty)
history.note_ja: Lake Bezymyannoye (about 40,000 m3) on the Kargaly glacier burst at about 02:15; dozens of homes filled with mud, over 1,000 evacuated, 5 hospitalised, no deaths; state of emergency declared in Almaty.

history.name_ja: January 2018 Arctic cold wave (-40 C)
history.where: Northern and central Kazakhstan incl. Astana
history.note_ja: Arctic cyclone brought temperatures near -40 C; the Health Ministry reported 223 people treated for frostbite, 73 admitted. Similar waves: winter 2012-13 (-40 to -46 C), Feb 2014, Jan-Feb 2021 (frostbite deaths in Kostanay Region).

history.name_ja: 2020 Sardoba dam failure (Uzbekistan) flooding of Maktaaral district, Turkistan Region
history.where: Maktaaral (Paxtaorol) district, Turkistan Region; dam in Sirdaryo Region, Uzbekistan
history.note_ja: 31,606 residents of 14 settlements evacuated in Kazakhstan, 5 settlements (6,127 people) fully flooded; deaths (4-6) were in Uzbekistan. EM-DAT 2020 flood total for Kazakhstan: 33,000 affected.

history.name_ja: 2021 Central Asia drought and heat wave (Mangystau, Kyzylorda, Turkistan)
history.where: Western and southern Kazakhstan (Mangystau, Kyzylorda, Turkistan, Atyrau)
history.note_ja: Drought from April 2021 caused mass livestock deaths (official 1,154 cattle in Mangystau; herders' estimates far higher), record 46.5 C on 7 July 2021, state of emergency in the Aral area of Kyzylorda (14 July); EU/IFRC: over 70,000 people affected.

history.name_ja: 2022 Kostanay Region forest fires (Auliekol)
history.where: Auliekol district, Kostanay Region
history.note_ja: About 43,000 ha burned (record), 108 houses destroyed, 1,841 people evacuated, state of emergency from 4 September; 10 injured reported; no confirmed deaths.

history.name_ja: 2023 Abai Region (Semey pine forest) wildfires
history.where: Abai Region (Semey ormany reserve), north-east Kazakhstan
history.note_ja: Lightning-ignited fires burned about 60,000 ha; at least 14-15 forestry workers and firefighters died; villages evacuated; the Minister of Emergency Situations was dismissed on 10 June.

history.name_ja: 2024 Uqturpan (Wushi) earthquake, Mw 7.0, Xinjiang-Kyrgyzstan border - strongly felt in Almaty
history.where: Epicentre 128 km WNW of Aykol (China), about 270 km from Almaty; felt across Almaty, Jetisu, Jambyl
history.note_ja: 3 deaths in Xinjiang; 74 injured of whom 67 in Kazakhstan (mostly people rushing out of buildings in Almaty at 00:09 local time). USGS us7000lsze Mw 7.0, 13 km deep.

history.name_ja: 2024 spring snowmelt floods (Kulsary, Petropavlovsk, Uralsk, Aktobe, Kostanay, Akmola, Pavlodar, East Kazakhstan)
history.where: 12 regions; worst in Atyrau (Kulsary), North Kazakhstan (Petropavlovsk), West Kazakhstan (Uralsk/Zhaiyk), Aktobe, Kostanay, Akmola (Atbasar)
history.note_ja: Largest disaster in 80 years (President Tokayev). MES: 96,472 evacuated by 10 April, 117,694 by 18 April, over 120,000 in total; IFRC: over 12,000 houses and 7,000 dachas flooded; 9,000+ houses to repair and 7,000-8,400 beyond repair. GDACS Orange flood alert FL-2024-000039-KAZ (28 Mar - 10 Apr). Damage is derived: government estimate of 237 bn KZT to restore destroyed housing / about 450 KZT per USD = about USD 530 M (housing only; assumption). Official death toll not confirmed (press figures contradictory).

KGZ.country_note_ja: Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous, landlocked country of 7.4 million whose people live in two valleys: the Chuy valley around Bishkek in the north and the Fergana rim (Osh, Jalal-Abad, Batken) in the south. ThinkHazard rates earthquake, landslide, urban flood and wildfire High nationwide; GEM estimates building losses of USD 31.6 M/yr with 85% of it in the south, and the 1911 Kemin (M8.0), 1992 Suusamyr (M7.3) and 2008 Nura (M6.6) earthquakes define the seismic benchmark. The most frequent killers are spring landslides and mudflows on loess slopes (1994, 2003, 2004, 2017), while winter brings extreme cold, Bishkek smog and, since 2023, an official energy emergency as the Toktogul reservoir runs low.

history.name_ja: 1885 Belovodskoe earthquake (Mw 6.9-7.6, MSK X), Chuy valley west of Bishkek
history.where: Belovodskoye (Belovodsk), Chuy valley, 45 km west of Bishkek
history.note_ja: Wikipedia list gives Mw 7.6, MMI X and 54 deaths; instrumental re-evaluation (Krueger et al. 2018) gives Mw 6.9. Pre-instrumental, not in USGS ComCat. The dedicated article page was not reachable (404) in this session.

history.name_ja: 1911 Kemin (Chon-Kemin / Kebin) earthquake, Mw 8.0
history.where: Chon-Kemin, Chilik and Chon-Aksu valleys (Chuy / Issyk-Kul regions), 37 km from Almaty
history.note_ja: 452 dead and 740 injured; more than 770 buildings destroyed in Verny (Almaty); 201 km of surface rupture. USGS ISC-GEM Mw 8.02 at 20 km depth (iscgem16958130); GEM profile prints M 8.2 with an asterisk (epicentre on the border). The largest instrumental earthquake in Central Asia.

history.name_ja: 1992 Suusamyr (Toluk) earthquake, Mw 7.3
history.where: Suusamyr valley / Toluk, 60 km ENE of Toktogul (Chuy-Jalal-Abad border), 116 km from Bishkek
history.note_ja: Wikipedia: about 75 deaths including 14 killed by landslides, MMI IX, reverse faulting; USGS usp0005cq0 Mwb 7.3, depth 27 km, with M6.6 and M6.3 aftershocks the same day. EM-DAT (OWID) 1992 earthquake totals: 58 deaths, 104,168 affected, 32,538 homeless, damage USD 161 M (annual total for Kyrgyzstan).

history.name_ja: 1994 spring landslides in Osh and Jalal-Abad regions (Kara-Taryk and other villages)
history.where: Loess foothills of Osh and Jalal-Abad regions (Uzgen, Aksy and other districts)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT (OWID) 1994 landslide totals: 162 deaths, 45,000 affected, 13,500 homeless, damage USD 36 M. ADRC databook lists a 14 April 1994 landslide event for Osh and Jalal-Abad regions; an MES official later told IRIN that 90 people died at Kara-Taryk alone in 1994 (search snippets). More than 20 landslides occurred in April 1994 after wet winter and minor quakes.

history.name_ja: 1998 Kugart river dam break and floods in Suzak district (Jalal-Abad)
history.where: Suzak and Jalal-Abad, Jalal-Abad Region; also Osh Region
history.note_ja: Torrential rains from 18 May 1998 raised the Kugart river, which broke a 100 m wide dam; 1 death, about 7,700 people left their homes (8,760 resettled), some 1,170-1,250 houses, 40 offices, 45 km of power lines and 40 km of the Jalal-Abad-Kara-Suu road destroyed, ~10,000 people affected (OCHA). ReliefWeb GLIDE FL-1998-000213-KGZ. EM-DAT 1998 flood: 1 death, 7,728 homeless, damage USD 2.4 M.

history.name_ja: 1998 Shakhimardan glacial lake outburst flood (Alay range, Batken Region / Uzbek enclave)
history.where: Shakhimardan (Shahimardan) catchment, Kadamjai district of Batken Region and the Uzbek enclave downstream
history.note_ja: Deadliest GLOF in Central Asia in at least 100 years: outburst of a thermokarst lake at the Archa-Bashy glacier released >50,000 m3; more than 100 deaths (Petrakov et al. 2020), most of them in the Uzbek enclave; Dartmouth Flood Observatory lists 93 deaths and 14,000 displaced. No cross-border warning was issued. Death toll uncertain (25 to >100 in different papers).
history.src_name: NHESS / Science of the Total Environment (search snippets)

history.name_ja: 2003 Kara-Taryk landslide (Uzgen district, Osh Region)
history.where: Kara-Taryk village, Uzgen district, Osh Region
history.note_ja: At least 38 killed (17 children, 13 women) when a saturated loess slope buried houses; EM-DAT (OWID) 2003 landslide totals: 38 deaths, 211 affected. ReliefWeb GLIDE SL-2003-000177-KGZ (Landslide - Apr 2003).

history.name_ja: 2004 Budalyk landslide (Alay district, Osh Region)
history.where: Budalyk village, Alay district, Osh Region
history.note_ja: Landslide killed 33 people (16 children) and injured 11; Bishkek appealed for international help. EM-DAT (OWID) 2004 landslide totals: 49 deaths, 18 injured (annual, several events). ReliefWeb GLIDE LS-2003-000177-KGZ (Landslides - Apr 2004).

history.name_ja: 2008 Nura earthquake, Mw 6.6-6.7 (Alay district, Osh Region)
history.where: Nura village, Alay district, Osh Region, near the Chinese border (Irkeshtam)
history.note_ja: Village of Nura destroyed; Wikipedia 75 dead and 150 injured; EM-DAT 74 deaths, 142 injured, 4,197 affected; GEM profile 74 deaths. USGS usp000gjd4 Mwc 6.7, depth 27 km. ReliefWeb GLIDE EQ-2008-000181-KGZ. Day of mourning 2008-10-07.

history.name_ja: December 2012 cold wave and heavy snow (lowest temperatures in 76 years; Bishkek state of emergency)
history.where: Northern Kyrgyzstan (Bishkek, Chuy, Talas, Naryn, Issyk-Kul); snow 2 m in Kara-Kulja (south)
history.note_ja: IFRC (22 Dec 2012): -30 to -35 C in the north, 16 dead and 50 injured, state of emergency declared in Bishkek on 18 Dec 2012; forecast cold until end-Feb 2013. EM-DAT (OWID) 2012 extreme-temperature totals: 16 deaths, 50 injured. Earlier the same year (Jan 2012) Bishkek had about 40 power failures a day during a very cold winter, and 15 homeless people died of hypothermia after the CHP boiler failed (search snippets). ReliefWeb GLIDE CW-2012-000209-KGZ.

history.name_ja: 2017 Ayu landslide (Uzgen district, Osh Region)
history.where: Ayu village, Uzgen district, Osh Region
history.note_ja: A landslide buried 6-7 houses early on 29 April 2017 killing all 24 people inside, including 9 children; 266 rescuers; 40 nearby families evacuated; the village had been evacuated in March for slope instability but residents returned; national day of mourning 30 April. EM-DAT (OWID) 2017 landslide totals: 24 deaths.

history.name_ja: Energy emergency 2023-2026: low Toktogul reservoir, winter power rationing (also 2008 and Feb 2022 blackouts)
history.where: Nationwide; Toktogul HPP (Naryn river) supplies about 40% of electricity
history.note_ja: Presidential decree put the energy sector under a state of emergency from 2023-08-01 to 2026-12-31 because of low Naryn inflows; Toktogul (total capacity 19.5 km3, 1,440 MW) held 10.8 km3 in Sep 2025 and 9.1 km3 in Jan 2026 (dead level ~5.5 km3); rolling-blackout warnings for winter 2025-26. Earlier episodes: Nov 2008 energy/water/food insecurity (ReliefWeb OT-2008-000238-KGZ) and regional power cuts in Feb 2022. Compounds the extreme-cold hazard for heating.

history.name_ja: 2024 Uqturpan (Wushi) earthquake, Mw 7.0, Kyrgyzstan-Xinjiang border
history.where: Epicentre in Uqturpan County, Xinjiang (41.26N 78.65E), 13 km deep; felt in Issyk-Kul, Bishkek and Almaty
history.note_ja: USGS us7000lsze Mww 7.0 at 18:09 UTC. 3 deaths in Xinjiang, 74 injured (67 in Kazakhstan), damage CNY 3.79 bn (USD 527 M) in China; MSK VI in Jeti-Oguz district (Issyk-Kul Region); residents of Bishkek and Almaty ran into the streets; no damage reported in Kyrgyzstan (chief seismologist). Deaths and damage are the China totals.

history.name_ja: 2024 spring-summer floods and mudflows (Osh, Jalal-Abad, Batken, Talas, Naryn)
history.where: Osh city and 23 villages of Osh Region, Jalal-Abad, Batken (Razzakov), Talas, Naryn; June mudflows in Jalal-Abad, Osh, Batken, Talas, Issyk-Kul
history.note_ja: Heavy rain 20-24 April 2024 (more rain in 8 days than a normal April): 103,901 people affected, 1 death, states of emergency in Osh, Jalal-Abad and Talas; 17-24 June mudflows affected >500 families and killed a 5-year-old in Batken (IFRC). DREF MDRKG019 CHF 488,376. Media counted 25 mudflow deaths in Kyrgyzstan in 2024 (search snippet). ReliefWeb GLIDE FL-2024-000053-KGZ.

history.name_ja: Bishkek winter smog (PM2.5 from household coal heating, inversions), heating season
history.where: Bishkek and the Chuy valley (also Osh in winter)
history.note_ja: Bishkek ranks among the top five most polluted cities during the heating season and exceeded WHO PM2.5 guidelines by up to 30 times in winter (ADB brief, Nov 2023); households and buildings not connected to the CHP network are the main source, the CHP plant itself <1% of PM2.5 (UNDP/UNICEF 2022). Smog fell 10-15% in winter 2023-24 with gas connections in 31 of 47 suburbs (ministry statement, Feb 2024). Chronic hazard, no death count.

extreme_cold.note: Not a ThinkHazard hazard; level is our assumption. Rationale: the January-February 2008 cold wave (below -20 C, coldest winter in 44 years) combined with a hydropower shortfall (low Nurek reservoir) into the costliest disaster in EM-DAT for Tajikistan (2,000,000 affected, USD 840 M damage, OWID/EM-DAT 'temperature' 2008); January 2013 saw -35 to -55 C in Murghob district (GBAO) with villages isolated for weeks. Lowland cities are milder (Dushanbe January mean 3.1 C, record low -26.6 C; Khujand 0.9 C, record -22.8 C), so the High rating reflects systemic vulnerability (winter electricity rationing, no district heating in many apartment blocks, mountain roads closed by snow and avalanches) rather than extreme temperatures in the capital.

flood.note: Spring rains on saturated loess trigger floods in Khatlon, Hisor and Rasht valleys March-May (1998, 2009, 2010, 2014, 2024 events were in April-May); snow- and glacier-melt peaks on the Vakhsh, Panj, Zeravshan and Syr Darya in June-July, when heat waves add GLOF/debris-flow floods (Barsem July 2015, Ayni July 2026).

urban_flood.note: Convective downpours and hail flood Dushanbe, Kulob and Khujand streets in spring; late-August storms (2023) and the Varzob/Luchob rivers also hit the capital's water intakes.

landslide.note: Mudflows (sel) and loess landslides April-June are the most frequent killers (about 40% of CoES incidents); glacier-melt debris flows in the Pamir July-August; snow avalanches on the Dushanbe-Khujand (Anzob) and Dushanbe-Khorog roads January-March (February 2023: 19 deaths).

heat.note: July peak: Dushanbe record 45.0 C, Khujand 45.9 C, Khatlon lowlands 46-47 C (Tajikhydromet warnings of +47 C in July 2025); electricity demand and water shortages rise together.

cold.note: January cold spells to -20 C in the valleys (2008: coldest in 44 years) and -35 to -55 C in Murghob (2013); hydropower rationing and road closures make winter a systemic risk.

haze.note: Dust storms from Afghanistan ('Afghanets') and the Aral/Kyzylkum June-October with Tajikhydromet dust warnings (May-June 2025); winter inversion smog in Dushanbe December-January; wildfire 'High' in ThinkHazard refers to summer grass fires.

water.note: Irrigation shortfalls on the Syr Darya and Zeravshan in late summer; winter electricity rationing when the Nurek reservoir is low (Nurek supplies about 70% of electricity); GDACS has logged multi-country agricultural droughts 2021-2024 and 2024-2026.

TJK.country_note_ja: Tajikistan is the most hazard-exposed and least resilient of the five Central Asian states: 93% mountainous, ThinkHazard rates river flood, urban flood, earthquake, landslide and wildfire High nationally, and GEM puts the seismic average annual loss at USD 25 M/yr (0.6 per mille of a USD 41 B building stock) with a 500-year loss of about USD 1.4 B. Earthquakes drive the catastrophic tail (1907 Karatag 12,000+ and 1949 Khait about 7,200 deaths, both through landslides; the Sarez Lake dam is a standing outburst hazard), while mudflows, flash floods and avalanches kill people almost every spring and summer (2010: 75; 2023: 21 + 19; 2024: 25). Global indices rate the country Medium (INFORM 2025 4.0, rank 79/191) to low-medium (WorldRiskIndex 2025 2.85, rank 135/193) because exposure of assets is small, but vulnerability and lack of coping capacity are the highest in the region, and the 2008 cold-wave/energy crisis showed how winter shocks cascade through the power system.

history.name_ja: 1907 Karatag (Qaratog) earthquake, Ms 7.4 / ISC-GEM Mw 7.44, MMI IX
history.where: Qaratog, Hisor range, Tajikistan-Uzbekistan border, about 100 km west of Dushanbe (USGS epicentre 39.22N 68.00E)
history.note_ja: Death toll 12,000-15,000 (Wikipedia; GEM lists 12,000). Wikipedia's infobox gives 'US$200 million' damage without a clear basis, so damage is left null. Largest catalogued event within 150 km of Dushanbe and Samarkand; anchors the Dushanbe/Hisor valley worst case.

history.name_ja: 1911 Sarez earthquake (Ms 7.4, ISC-GEM Mw 7.23) and Usoi landslide dam - formation of Sarez Lake
history.where: Rushon District, GBAO (Bartang/Murghab valleys)
history.note_ja: Casualty estimates 90-302 (EM-DAT 90). The 2 km3 Usoi landslide created the world's tallest dam (567 m) impounding about 16-17 km3; a future outburst would threaten the Bartang-Panj-Amu Darya valley downstream (World Bank/STUCKY studies; dam survived the 2015 M7.2 without visible damage). The lake is a standing cross-border hazard item for Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.

history.name_ja: 1949 Khait (Hoit) earthquake, Mw 7.5, and the Khait rock avalanche / Yasman valley loess flowslides
history.where: Khait (Hoit), Rasht (Gharm) valley, Districts of Republican Subordination; USGS epicentre 43 km ENE of Rasht
history.note_ja: Deaths disputed: about 7,200 (recent study: about 800 by the Khait landslide, 4,000 by the Yasman flowslide), published range 5,000-28,000; GEM's profile lists 3,500. Most fatalities came from earthquake-triggered loess flowslides, not shaking. USGS ISC-GEM Mw 7.5, 20 km deep, with M6.1-6.9 aftershocks the same day.

history.name_ja: 1985 Kayrakkum (Qayroqqum) earthquake, Mw 5.8-5.9, MMI IX
history.where: Kayrakkum (Guliston) and Ghafurov, 15-25 km east of Khujand, Sughd Region
history.note_ja: 29 dead, more than 80 injured, 8,000 homeless; 90% of multi-storey brick buildings in Kayrakkum destroyed, Kayrakkum reservoir embankments damaged, carpet factory collapse; damage USD 200 M (1985 dollars, Wikipedia/NGDC). USGS usp0002ks3 Mw 5.8, 16 km deep, 17 km from Khujand.

history.name_ja: 1989 Gissar (Hisor) earthquake, mb 5.3, and the Sharora loess flowslides
history.where: Sharora and two neighbouring villages, Hisor district, 13 km west of Dushanbe
history.note_ja: Local date 23 January (22 January 23:02 UTC). Nearly all 274 deaths were caused by liquefaction-type loess flowslides that buried Sharora; MMI VII; damage USD 24 M (Wikipedia/NGDC). Deadliest earthquake of 1989 worldwide and the key quake-landslide cascade near the capital.

history.name_ja: 1992 floods and mudflows in southern Tajikistan (EM-DAT annual total; civil-war year)
history.where: Khatlon (Kulob, Vakhsh valley) and other lowland districts; EM-DAT country-year total
history.note_ja: EM-DAT (OWID mirror) 1992: flood deaths 1,346, 63,500 affected, USD 300 M damage, plus landslide deaths 243 (USD 24.1 M) - the deadliest flood year on record for Tajikistan, during the first year of the civil war when response capacity collapsed. Event-level details could not be verified in this session.

history.name_ja: 2008 cold wave and energy crisis (compound disaster): coldest winter in 44 years, hydropower shortfall, food insecurity
history.where: Nationwide; worst in Dushanbe (power cut to residential areas, no district heating) and rural lowlands; GBAO and mountains stayed frozen into March
history.note_ja: Temperatures below -20 C from mid-January, low water in the Nurek reservoir, villages on 1-3 hours of electricity per day, Dushanbe without heating; UN/Red Cross flash appeal about USD 25 M; EM-DAT lists 2,000,000 affected and USD 840 M damage (temperature), followed by the 2008 drought/food crisis (800,000 affected). Deaths were reported in hospitals and maternity wards but no verified total exists (EM-DAT 0).

history.name_ja: 2010 spring floods and mudflows (25 March - 7 May), Kulob/Vose/Muminobod and 21 districts
history.where: Khatlon (Kulob, Vose, Muminobod, Khuroson) and districts across the country
history.note_ja: Heavy rains 25 March-5 May 2010 caused floods and mudflows in 21 districts (5,288 affected, more than 1,000 houses, 50 km of mudflow-protection structures destroyed per UNCT/CoES); the 7 May Kulob flood added most of the deaths. EM-DAT 2010 flood total: 75 deaths, USD 204 M damage.

history.name_ja: 2015 Barsem debris flow (heat-driven glacier/snowmelt, Shughnon district, GBAO): Gunt river dammed, Pamir Highway cut
history.where: Barsem and Kolkhozobod villages, Shughnon district, 15 km from Khorog, GBAO
history.note_ja: Debris flows of about 4.2 million m3 from a periglacial source between 16 and 24 July 2015 after a heat wave; about 80 houses destroyed, 1,100 people in need, the Gunt dammed into a 2 km lake (still exists as Barsemkul), the Pamir Highway and Khorog's power supply cut. Deaths: 6 across GBAO in the July 2015 mudflows per UN situation reports (the Barsem flow itself is reported without fatalities); EM-DAT 2015 landslide deaths 10. May 2015 floods in Khatlon/Rasht (1,776 affected) preceded it.

history.name_ja: 2015 Murghab (Sarez) earthquake, Mw 7.2, Sarez-Karakul fault, GBAO
history.where: Western Murghob and Rushon districts, GBAO; epicentre 104 km W of Murghob, 5 km from the 1911 Sarez epicentre
history.note_ja: 2 killed by rock falls, more than 14 injured; 1,327 houses damaged or destroyed and about 7,962 displaced (CoES via RAPID, 12 Dec 2015); the Usoi dam showed no visible damage. Felt at MMI II in Dushanbe. EM-DAT damage USD 5 M.

history.name_ja: 2023 Khorog and Rushan avalanches (heavy snow, 15-19 February), GBAO
history.where: Khorog city (15 deaths), Shughnon and Vanj districts; 38 avalanches in Rushan in one day; Dushanbe-Khorog-Murghab highway closed; one death on the Dushanbe-Khujand road in Varzob
history.note_ja: Snow avalanches (counted here under landslide/mass movement). Toll reported as 15-16 (16 Feb), 18 (18 Feb) and 19-20 for 15-19 February by CoES/Interfax/Reuters; no final figure found. Four houses destroyed and about 40 damaged in Khorog.

history.name_ja: August 2023 torrential rains: flash floods, mudflows and landslides around Dushanbe (Vahdat, Rudaki, Varzob)
history.where: Vahdat (17 deaths), Rudaki and Varzob (Ajuk gorge) districts next to Dushanbe; damage also in Hisor, Rasht, Sangvor, Tojikobod and Devashtich
history.note_ja: Rain on 27-28 August 2023 triggered mudflows and flash floods; toll rose from 13 (28 Aug) to 21 (30 Aug, CoES to AFP), a newborn among the dead; the Dushanbe-Vahdat-Lakhsh highway was damaged. CoES states mudflows cause about 40% of all incidents and deaths every year.

history.name_ja: 2024 mudflow and flood season (May-August): Kulob, Varzob, Khatlon and Sughd - 25 deaths in the year
history.where: Kulob city (3 deaths, 1-2 May), Varzob (1 death, 5 May), Khuroson/Khatlon (14 May), Sughd (11-13 June), repeated GDACS flood alerts 4-6 May, 25-27 May, 11-13 Jun, 13-15 Jul, 4-6 Aug 2024
history.note_ja: Recurrent spring-summer mudflows: June 2022 mudflows damaged several districts, 2024 claimed 25 lives nationwide (Times of Central Asia citing CoES), 2025 saw floods in Kulob (GDACS 9-11 April 2025) and dust storms, and July 2026 flash floods hit Ayni (672 households). Damage totals are not published consistently; GDACS floods are all 'Green' alerts.
history.src_name: GDACS / Times of Central Asia / Asia-Plus

history.name_ja: 2025 Rasht earthquake, Mw 5.8 (USGS yellow alert), Rasht and Tojikobod districts
history.where: 42 km ESE of Rasht, 8 km deep; damage in Rasht and Tojikobod districts (DRS), felt at intensity 3 in Dushanbe
history.note_ja: 1 child killed, 16 injured; 67 homes destroyed, 195 partially and 186 lightly damaged, about 4,004 people affected (CoES/IFRC DREF MDRTJ036); damage 17.78 M somoni (about USD 1.66 M). Verification of a 'July 2025 Rasht/Jirgatol earthquake': USGS lists only M4.5 events near Rasht on 17 June and 12 July 2025 (GDACS Green), so the damaging 2025 event is this 13 April shock; the July 2025 reports appear to refer to aftershock-level tremors.

history.name_ja: Dushanbe seismic hazard: intensity IX zoning (MSK-64), Hissar-Kokshaal and Ilyak-Vakhsh faults, loess site effects
history.where: Dushanbe city and the Hisor valley
history.note_ja: Official zonation (1978 maps underlying the Tajik building code) assigns intensity IX to most of the city; the Hissar-Kokshaal fault runs 10-15 km north and the Ilyak-Vakhsh fault 20-25 km south. Site-amplification studies (Hakimov et al., Geosciences 2021) identify critical areas on soft sediments; 2025 InSAR work suggests the Ilyak fault creeps at the surface, lowering but not removing the large-event concern. Reference shocks: 1907 Karatag M7.4 (100 km), 1930 Dushanbe M6.3 (175 deaths), 1989 Gissar (13 km). GEM 475-year PGA for the Dushanbe-Hisor area is in the 0.2-0.5 g class; GEM AAL for Dushanbe city USD 4.6 M/yr plus DRS 6.5 M/yr (44% of the national 25.3 M). USGS counts 50 M5+ events within 150 km of Dushanbe since 1950.

Assumed 'Medium' from Tashkent climate records (January mean daily minimum -1.3 C, record low -29.5 C in December, -28 C in January; Wikipedia climate table) and from the January 2023 cold wave (about -20 C in Tashkent, reported as the coldest in roughly 50 years, with gas and electricity outages; search_snippet, bne IntelliNews / Interfax). Karakalpakstan and the north-west are colder (continental desert winters); the Fergana Valley and the south are milder. The main risk driver is energy-supply failure during cold spells rather than temperature alone.

flood.note: Snowmelt plus spring rain; Uzhydromet flood/mudflow warnings for foothill districts cluster between mid-February and June (Chirchik, Syr Darya tributaries, Zarafshan); the Sardoba dam failure was on 1 May 2020.

urban_flood.note: Short intense spring thunderstorms overwhelm storm drains in Tashkent and valley cities; occasional autumn (Oct-Nov) events.

landslide.note: Mudflows (sel) and landslides in loess foothills after rain-on-snow; avalanches on the Kamchik Pass in February-March; glacier-lake outbursts in July (Shohimardon 1998).

heat.note: Peak July (Tashkent all-time 44.6 C on 18 Jul 1997; 44.3 C on 19 Jul 2026); abnormal heat increasingly from late May (May 2025 among the three hottest on record).

cold.note: Continental winters; the January 2023 cold wave (about -20 C in Tashkent) coincided with gas and power failures.

haze.note: Winter inversion smog over Tashkent and the Fergana Valley (coal/gas heating, traffic) plus dust storms from the Aral/Kyzylkum deserts in autumn and spring (record storm 4-5 Nov 2021).

water.note: Irrigation-season shortages on the lower Amu Darya (Khorezm, Karakalpakstan) and Zarafshan in low-snow years (2000-01, 2021, 2023); Aral Sea desiccation is chronic.

UZB.country_note_ja: Uzbekistan is a doubly landlocked, mostly arid country of about 38 million people whose population and industry concentrate in the seismically active Tashkent oasis and the Fergana Valley, both rated High by ThinkHazard for earthquake, river and urban flood, landslide, extreme heat and water scarcity. GEM estimates an average annual earthquake building loss of 146 M USD (0.39 per mille of a 376 B USD building stock), with over half of it in the Fergana Valley provinces, and a 500-year loss of about 8.9 B USD. Recent disasters have been hydro-meteorological and infrastructural rather than seismic: the Sardoba dam failure (May 2020, about 70,000 evacuated), record heat (2021, 2023, 2025, 2026), the November 2021 dust storm and the January 2023 cold wave that collapsed gas and power supply in Tashkent.

history.name_ja: 1902 Andijan earthquake (Ms 6.4, Fergana Valley)
history.where: Andijan Region (Fergana Valley)
history.note_ja: Deadliest earthquake in Uzbekistan: city of Andijan levelled, over 40,000 homes destroyed, MMI IX; casualty estimates 700-4,880 (Wikipedia), 4,880 in the GEM profile. Absent from the USGS ComCat catalogue.

history.name_ja: 1966 Tashkent earthquake (M5.2, city centre destroyed)
history.where: Tashkent city
history.note_ja: Shallow (3-8 km) Mw 5.2 shock under central Tashkent at 05:23 local time; over 80% of the city and 78,000-95,000 mostly adobe homes destroyed, 200,000-300,000 homeless. Official toll 15 (GEM lists 10); other estimates up to 200. Led to Soviet-style rebuilding and the Institute of Seismology. USGS ISC-GEM entry: Mw 5.31, 9 km NNW of Tashkent.

history.name_ja: 1976 Gazli earthquakes (Ms 7.0 on 8 April and 17 May, Bukhara Region)
history.where: Gazli gas field, Bukhara Region (desert north-west of Bukhara)
history.note_ja: Two Ms 7.0 shocks six weeks apart (USGS usp0000ft0, usp0000gcj), in a previously quiet platform area and widely attributed to gas extraction (induced seismicity); intensity 9-10 MSK at Gazli, town largely rebuilt. Casualty figures not found in reachable sources (Soviet-era reporting).

history.name_ja: 1984 Gazli earthquake (Mw 7.0, Bukhara Region)
history.where: Gazli, Bukhara Region; felt VII in Bukhara, VI in Samarkand, IV in Tashkent
history.note_ja: USGS impact text: at least 100 injured, extensive damage (IX) in the Gazli area, damage VIII at Dzhangeldy and VII in the Bukhara area. An ADRC databook row (search_snippet, headings not visible) suggests about 100 deaths and thousands homeless; unconfirmed.

history.name_ja: 1998 Shohimardon glacier-lake outburst flood and mudflow (Fergana Region enclave)
history.where: Shohimardon (Uzbek enclave in Kyrgyzstan) and Yordon, Fergana Region
history.note_ja: Deadliest glacial-lake outburst flood in Central Asia in at least a century: a debris flow from the Kyrgyz headwaters hit the enclave at night; OCHA-sourced database gives 95 dead and 3,500 affected, ADRC 104 dead and about 100 houses collapsed, contemporary press 82-93. No cross-border warning was issued.
history.src_name: Water Unites CA / Science of the Total Environment summary (search)

history.name_ja: 2000-2001 drought (Amu Darya low flows; Karakalpakstan and Khorezm)
history.where: Lower Amu Darya (Karakalpakstan, Khorezm), nationwide irrigation
history.note_ja: Two consecutive low-water years; ReliefWeb disaster entries 'Uzbekistan: Drought - Aug 2000' and 'Jun 2001'. Rice and cotton losses in the lower reaches; Karakalpakstan supplies about half of national rice (IWPR, search_snippet).

history.name_ja: 2011 Fergana Valley earthquake (Mw 6.1, Kyrgyz border near Fergana)
history.where: Fergana Region (Fergana city, Margilan, Hamza); felt IV in Tashkent
history.note_ja: Reverse-faulting shock on the Pamir-Fergana boundary. USGS: at least 13 killed and 86 injured in Fergana, several buildings destroyed, a hospital severely damaged; Wikipedia gives 14 dead in Uzbekistan and one in Khujand, Tajikistan; at least 800 houses damaged.

history.name_ja: 2020 Sardoba reservoir dam failure (Sirdaryo Region; flooding into Kazakhstan)
history.where: Sardoba, Oqoltin and Mirzaobod districts of Sirdaryo Region; Maktaaral district of Turkistan Region (KAZ)
history.note_ja: Section of the 2016-2017 earth-fill dam (reservoir built for 404 M USD) breached after heavy rain and wind; ECHO Daily Flash of 4 May 2020: 50 injured and at least 70,000 evacuated from 22 villages, 5,400 evacuated in Kazakhstan. Wikipedia: 4 dead (6 by another source), 1 missing, 2,570 houses and 76 apartment blocks destroyed, 1,781 houses damaged; nine officials prosecuted. Damage estimate not found.

history.name_ja: 2021 heat wave and drought (Tashkent 42.6 C in June, 41.5 C on 6 July)
history.where: Nationwide; worst water shortages in Khorezm and Karakalpakstan
history.note_ja: June 2021 was then the hottest June on record in Tashkent (42.6 C early June); a low-snow year brought irrigation shortages, harvest losses and limited vegetable supply (UNESCAP), and the Ministry of Water Resources had warned of shortages in February 2021. The summer heat over Kazakhstan was later linked to the November dust storm.

history.name_ja: 2021 Tashkent dust storm (worst since records began in 1871)
history.where: Tashkent and Tashkent, Sirdaryo and Jizzakh regions
history.note_ja: Dust reached Tashkent on the evening of 4 Nov 2021: particulate levels about 30 times the limit at 21:00 (up to 50 times by one study), visibility down to 200 m, about 4,000 ambulance calls for respiratory distress nationwide; Uzhydromet called it unprecedented in 150 years of observations. NASA Earth Observatory imaged the plume.

history.name_ja: January 2023 cold wave and energy crisis (Tashkent about -20 C, gas and power cuts)
history.where: Tashkent and most regions; worst in the capital
history.note_ja: Abnormal cold from about 12 January with gas imports from Turkmenistan halted (12-21 Jan) and electricity imports cut 20%; rolling blackouts, failed transformers, heating loss in apartment blocks, residents protesting at energy facilities on 18 Jan; President dismissed the Tashkent mayor on 16 Jan; electricity exports to Afghanistan suspended. Meteorologists called it the coldest spell in about 50 years. Casualties not reported.

history.name_ja: June 2023 heat wave (hottest June on record in Tashkent)
history.where: Tashkent and lowland regions
history.note_ja: Prolonged heat made June 2023 the hottest June in Tashkent's record, ahead of June 2021; July 2023 ran 2-3 C above normal. Linked to the wider 2023 Asia heat wave.

history.name_ja: 2024 spring floods and mudflows (Surkhandarya mudflow; nationwide mudflow warnings in April; Kamchik Pass landslide in May)
history.where: Kumkurgan district (Surkhandarya); foothill districts of nine regions; Kamchik Pass (Tashkent-Fergana road)
history.note_ja: 21 March 2024: hill runoff flooded a mahalla in Kumkurgan, 360 people moved to relatives, no casualties; 14-23 April 2024 Uzhydromet mudflow/flood warnings for Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, Samarkand, Navoi, Jizzakh, Tashkent, Namangan, Fergana and Andijan; May 2024 landslide closed the Kamchik Pass road (no casualties). Uzbekistan also sent aid to Kazakhstan's 2024 floods. No large-loss flood occurred in Uzbekistan in 2024 in reachable sources.

history.name_ja: 2025 heat wave (hottest and driest May on record; early-July heat with about 250,000 emergency calls)
history.where: Nationwide; Tashkent near 41 C in mid-May
history.note_ja: Uzhydromet ranked May 2025 among the three hottest Mays in the national record and abnormally dry (near the 170-year May record in Tashkent); forecasts of 45 C in the south; a headline reports nearly 250,000 emergency calls during the early-July 2025 heat (details not seen).

history.name_ja: July 2026 heat wave (Tashkent 44.3 C, 0.3 C below the all-time record; records in the Fergana Valley)
history.where: Tashkent, Fergana Valley capitals, southern regions
history.note_ja: Uzhydromet attributed the mid-July 2026 heat to a thermal depression; Tashkent reached 44.3 C on 19 July (record 44.6 C on 18 Jul 1997) and the Fergana Valley regional capitals broke their maxima two to three times; Euronews reported a 'rare 48 C heatwave' (figure not confirmed).

regions.hazard_scope_ja: city division (ThinkHazard 'Almaty City area', code 37157); Almaty Region (Almatinskaya, 1716) levels are listed in hazards_alt and hz_note
regions.pop_src: Almaty city 2.35 M (1 Jan 2026 estimate) + Almaty Region 1,520,216 (2023, after the 2022 split of Jetisu) - Wikipedia infoboxes citing stat.gov.kz (third_party)
regions.desc_ja: Largest city and business hub of Kazakhstan, built on the alluvial fans of the Trans-Ili Alatau (Tien Shan) at 700-1,000 m, with Almaty Region (Ili valley, Kapshagay reservoir, Konayev, Talgar, Esik) around it. The city was destroyed by earthquakes in 1887 and 1911 and by a mudflow in 1921; mudflow corridors run through the Malaya/Bolshaya Almatinka, Kargalinka, Talgar and Esik valleys. Dense Soviet-era and newer high-rise housing sits partly on loess and alluvium that amplify shaking.

extreme_cold.note: Assumed Medium: January mean about -5 C with cold spells to -30 C; milder than the north (Astana High).

regions.hz_note_ja: The city division is rated Very low for river and urban flood because the city sits on fans above the Ili plain, but the surrounding Almaty Region is High for river flood (Ili, Kaskelen, Talgar, Esik rivers, reservoir and small-dam failures such as Kyzylagash 2010) and High for landslide, which here means debris/mud flows: the 1921 flow killed about 500 people and the Medeu (1973) and Bolshaya Almatinka dams exist to stop repeats; the 2015 Kargaly moraine-lake outburst shows the summer glacial-melt mechanism. Earthquake High reflects the 1887 (Mw 7.3-7.7) and 1911 Kemin (Mw 8.0, 37 km away) events; GEM attributes USD 7.5 M of the national 16.3 M annual building loss to Almaty city and region. Wildfire High and water scarcity apply to the region's steppe and the Ili-Balkhash basin rather than the city; winter smog (coal heating, inversions) is the chronic air-quality issue.

flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: the 2010 Kyzylagash dam failure (43 deaths, 211 injured, EM-DAT USD 34.6 M; in the Aksu district that belonged to Almaty Region until 2022) and the spring floods of the Ili, Kaskelen, Talgar and Esik rivers. The city itself is rated Very low; losses concentrate in the region's lowland towns and dachas.

scen.10: Spring snowmelt overtops small irrigation dams and floods lowland villages and dacha areas along the Ili and Kaskelen; a few hundred evacuated
scen.50: 2010 Kyzylagash-type dam failure: a town of 2,000-5,000 people inundated within hours, dozens of deaths possible at night
scen.100: Several foothill rivers in flood at once after rain-on-snow; bridges and the A-2/A-3 highways cut for days, Konayev and Talgar suburbs flooded
scen.500: Combined rain-on-snow and glacial melt; multiple small dams fail, Ili lowlands under 1-2 m for weeks
scen.1000: Failure or emergency release at a major reservoir (Kapshagay-type) flooding the Ili valley downstream of the city; city core still largely dry

flood.method_ja: loss = loss_max x k. k is the shape of the WRI Aqueduct national riverine urban-damage curve for Kazakhstan (2010 baseline; USD 7069.5 M at 10 yr to 20544.6 M at 1,000 yr), so k[1000]=1. loss_max = an assumed regional share (5%) of the national 1,000-year Aqueduct damage. Depth, area, affected population and downtime scale with the same k (population and downtime with k^2.5 in the app). This is a screening model, not a hydraulic study.
assumptions_ja: Regional share 5% of the national Aqueduct damage is assumed: the region holds about 19% of the population but most of it lives on fans and terraces above the rivers.
The 2010 event (USD 35 M) is treated as roughly a 50-year event; a 1,000-year event is assumed about 30 times larger because of reservoir and urban-fringe exposure.
Aqueduct values are 2010-baseline urban damage without local flood defences; actual protection (dams, levees) is not modelled.
Population affected and downtime scale with k^2.5 as in the app.

urban_flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: short, intense summer thunderstorms and spring melt that flood underpasses, the lower (northern) districts and the Esentai/Malaya Almatinka embankments for hours; no public loss statistics, so every value is assumed.

scen.10: Annual-scale: 20-40 cm on low streets and underpasses for a few hours, traffic jams, a few basements flooded
scen.50: Half-day inundation of the northern districts and ring roads; metro entrances and parking garages sandbagged
scen.100: Storm plus river-channel overflow: 0.5-0.8 m in lower districts, power cuts, one to two days of disruption
scen.500: Multi-day event with drainage failure and mud on roads, retail and logistics halted in the north
scen.1000: Drainage and river channels blocked by debris from simultaneous mudflows

urban_flood.method_ja: Loss is a rough product of disrupted business days and affected area; not based on a public loss record.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed at about USD 75 M per day of city-wide disruption over two days.
Affected population 3% of the metro area at k=1 (lower districts).

quake.anchor_ja: National loss curve: GEM Country Seismic Risk Profile (building loss). GEM's regional split gives Almaty Region USD 5.7 M/yr and Almaty city 1.8 M/yr of the national 16.3 M/yr, i.e. 46%; this share is applied to the national curve (GEM's 'Almaty Region' still includes today's Jetisu Region).

scen.10: M5 within 100 km (e.g., 2011 Turgen M5.1, 2014 Cholpon-Ata M5.0): felt by all, people leave buildings, minor cracks
scen.50: M5.5-6 under the foothills (1988 Talgar M5.7 type, 56 km): non-structural damage, some old brick buildings damaged, elevators stopped
scen.100: M6-6.5 within 100 km (1990 Baisorun M6.4 type): damage to pre-1980 masonry housing, several collapses, days of power and gas interruption
scen.500: 1887 Verny-type Mw 7.3-7.7 on the Trans-Ili Alatau front: widespread collapse of unreinforced housing, thousands of casualties, weeks without services
scen.1000: 1911 Kemin-type Mw 8.0 at 37 km: most of the old city destroyed as in 1911, months of recovery

quake.method_ja: loss = GEM national building-loss curve for Kazakhstan (USD 13.6 M at 10 yr, 162.5 M at 50 yr, 332.3 M at 100 yr, about 1,100 M at 500 yr, about 1,700 M at 1,000 yr; residential+commercial+industrial, 2025 USD) x share. share is the region's fraction of GEM's regional AAL split. k is an assumed relative intensity used only for affected population and downtime.
assumptions_ja: Share 46% from GEM's loss-by-region chart; Almaty city alone would be 11%.
Affected population 30% of the metro at k=1 (people displaced or without services after an M8-class event).
Downtime up to 60 days for businesses in damaged buildings; modern code-conforming offices may reopen in days.
USGS ComCat lists 23 M5+ events within 150 km since 1950 (2 of M6+), the largest ever the 1911 Kemin Mw 8.02.

landslide.anchor_ja: Anchor: the 1921 Malaya Almatinka mudflow (about 10 million m3, about 500 deaths) and the 2015 Kargaly moraine-lake outburst (about 40,000 m3, 1,000+ evacuated, no deaths). Mudflow corridors: Malaya and Bolshaya Almatinka, Kargalinka, Aksai, Talgar, Esik.

scen.10: Small debris flow or lake outburst in one valley (2015 type): roads and dozens of houses in the foothill districts damaged, no deaths
scen.50: Mudflow of 1-3 million m3 reaching the upper city if a retention dam is bypassed; dozens of houses destroyed, casualties possible
scen.100: Simultaneous flows in two valleys after a heat wave plus rain; Medeu/Bolshaya Almatinka dams fill, upper districts evacuated
scen.500: 1973-type flow with a dam near capacity; partial overtopping, 1921-scale damage to the upper city
scen.1000: 1921-type catastrophe with dam failure: central districts along the river buried in mud, hundreds of deaths

landslide.method_ja: Loss scaled from an assumed USD 400 M for a dam-overtopping event affecting the upper (richest) districts; return periods are expert assumptions informed by the 1921/1973/2015 record.
assumptions_ja: The Medeu dam (capacity raised after 1973) is assumed to hold up to roughly the 500-year flow.
Glacier retreat and growing moraine lakes make summer outbursts more frequent, so the 10-year event is set to a 2015-type flow.
Loss at k=1 is assumed (no public estimate); affected population 4% of the metro area (foothill districts).

heat.anchor_ja: Anchor: July heat waves; the 2021 regional heat (46.5 C record in the south on 2021-07-07) reached about 40 C in Almaty. No public loss data; values assumed.

scen.10: 3-5 days above 36 C: power demand peaks, outdoor work limited at midday
scen.50: A week above 38 C with night minima above 25 C: heat illness in the elderly, water-supply pressure drops
scen.100: 10 days above 40 C: rolling outages, glacier melt triggers mudflow alerts
scen.500: Two weeks above 40 C with wildfire smoke
scen.1000: Record 43-44 C heat dome combined with regional drought and fires

heat.method_ja: Loss is an assumed productivity and outage cost; affected population is the share exposed to heat-health risk.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed at USD 80 M (lost output and power outages).
Affected population 20% (elderly, outdoor workers, poorly cooled housing).

history.name_ja: 1887 Verny earthquake (Mw 7.3-7.7, MSK X) destroys Almaty
history.scope_ja: Almaty city and foothills
history.note_ja: At least 332 killed in Verny (161 in the Almatinka villages) plus 154 in mountain landslides; about 250 aftershocks; thrust fault under the Trans-Ili Alatau. Pre-1900, not in USGS ComCat.
history.jp_ja: Defines the design earthquake for the city: expect prolonged aftershocks and landslide-blocked mountain roads; foreign staff should have assembly points away from old masonry.

history.name_ja: 1889 Chilik earthquake (Mw 7.9-8.0), east of Almaty
history.scope_ja: Chilik valley, Tien Shan - Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, China
history.note_ja: At least 92 dead across three countries; one of the largest known intracontinental earthquakes; macroseismic magnitude estimate.
history.jp_ja: Shows that M8-class ruptures occur on several faults around the city, not only the 1911 one.

history.name_ja: 1911 Kemin (Chon-Kemin) earthquake, Mw 8.0, 37 km from Almaty
history.scope_ja: Almaty and Chon-Kemin valley (Kyrgyzstan)
history.note_ja: 452 dead, 740 injured, more than 770 buildings (almost the whole city) destroyed; USGS ISC-GEM Mw 8.02, depth 20 km; largest event within 150 km of Almaty in the catalogue.
history.jp_ja: Worst-case scenario for Almaty offices: total loss of older buildings, weeks without utilities; the embassy's Almaty office and most foreign firms are in the central districts built after 1911.

history.name_ja: 1921 Malaya Almatinka mudflow (about 500 deaths)
history.scope_ja: Small Almaty valley and central Almaty
history.note_ja: Rain-triggered flow of about 10 million m3 killed about 500 of 45,000 residents and destroyed much of the city; led to the Medeu dam. Day of month unverified.
history.jp_ja: Mudflow corridors still pass through the upscale upper districts (Medeu, Gornyi Gigant) where many expatriates live.

history.name_ja: 1963 Lake Issyk outburst and mudflow (Esik)
history.scope_ja: Esik (Issyk) valley, Almaty Region
history.note_ja: A landslide destroyed the natural dam of Lake Issyk; the resulting flood damaged the town of Esik. Death toll not given by Wikipedia (secondary sources cite hundreds; unverified); day of month unverified.
history.jp_ja: Example of a natural dam failure on the regional side; Esik is 50 km from the city on the A-351 corridor.

history.name_ja: 1973 Medeu mudflow stopped by the Medeu dam
history.scope_ja: Medeu valley above Almaty
history.note_ja: Glacial-lake outburst flow; the just-completed dam captured 3.8 million m3 of sediment and saved the city.
history.jp_ja: Proof that the retention dams work for a 50-100-year flow; a larger event or a blocked spillway remains the residual risk.

history.name_ja: 1990 Baisorun (Tyup) earthquake, Mw 6.4, 98 km from Almaty
history.scope_ja: Kungey Alatau, Kyrgyzstan-Kazakhstan border
history.note_ja: USGS ComCat usp0004gu0: Mw 6.4, depth 19 km, 35 km NW of Tyup; the largest regional event since 1978 (Zhalanash-Tyup Ms 7.1, 143 km).
history.jp_ja: Typical 100-year-scale event: strong shaking in the city without collapses; triggers evacuation of offices and schools.

history.name_ja: 2010 Kyzylagash dam failure flood (Aksu district, then Almaty Region)
history.scope_ja: Kyzylagash village, Aksu district (now Jetisu Region)
history.note_ja: Dam burst about 22:00 after rain and sudden snowmelt; at least 43 killed, 211 injured, over 1,000 evacuated; EM-DAT 2010 Kazakhstan flood total 44 deaths, 29,200 affected, USD 34.6 M; officials detained.
history.jp_ja: Small irrigation dams above villages are the main regional flood risk; check dam locations upstream of any site or staff housing.

history.name_ja: 2015 Kargaly moraine-lake outburst mudflow, Nauryzbay district
history.scope_ja: Kargalinka river - Chapaevo, Kargaly, Kamenka (Almaty)
history.note_ja: Lake Bezymyannoye (about 40,000 m3) burst at about 02:15; dozens of homes filled with mud, over 1,000 evacuated, 5 hospitalised, no deaths; city state of emergency. The Kargaly dam held.
history.jp_ja: Night-time event: staff in the western foothill suburbs need alert channels that wake them (SMS 112 arrived late for some).

history.name_ja: 2024 Uqturpan (Wushi) earthquake, Mw 7.0, felt strongly in Almaty
history.scope_ja: Epicentre in Xinjiang near Kyrgyzstan, about 270 km from Almaty; 67 injured in Kazakhstan
history.note_ja: Struck at 00:09 Almaty time; 3 deaths in Xinjiang, 74 injured of whom 67 in Kazakhstan, mostly people rushing out of apartment blocks; USGS us7000lsze Mw 7.0, 13 km deep; the Mass Alert system and SMS reached only part of the population.
history.jp_ja: Showed panic evacuation of high-rises in winter at night: plan warm clothing, stairwell discipline and assembly points for staff housing.

flood.note_ja: Snowmelt on the Ili and foothill rivers April-June; small-dam failures after rain-on-snow in March-April (2010).

landslide.note_ja: Rain-triggered flows May-June; glacier and moraine-lake outbursts during July-August heat (1921, 1973, 2015 all in July).

heat.note_ja: July peak, about 40 C in the city.

cold.note_ja: January mean about -5 C; cold spells to -30 C; black ice.

haze.note_ja: Winter coal-smoke smog under inversions (November-February); wildfire smoke from the steppe in July-August.

water.note_ja: Irrigation shortfalls in the Ili-Balkhash basin in late summer.

regions.hazard_scope_ja: ThinkHazard admin-1 level (Akmolinskaya, code 1714); ThinkHazard has no separate Astana/Nur-Sultan division, the Tselinograd district (37174) that surrounds the capital is given in hazards_alt
regions.pop_src: Astana 1,700,385 (1 Sep 2026) + Akmola Region 785,708 (2022-01-01) - Wikipedia infoboxes citing stat.gov.kz (third_party)
regions.desc_ja: The capital (since 1997) on the Yesil/Ishim river in the flat northern steppe at 350 m, with the surrounding Akmola Region (Kokshetau, Atbasar, Stepnogorsk; grain farming). The climate is extreme continental: January mean -14.5 C with a record -51.6 C (1893) and summer heat above 35 C. The main hazards are spring snowmelt floods on the Yesil, Zhabay, Nura and Seleti rivers, blizzards and cold waves that stress district heating, and steppe/forest fires; seismicity is negligible (no catalogued event within 150 km of Astana).

extreme_cold.note: Assumed High: January mean -14.5 C, record -51.6 C (1893), -40 C spells in 2012-13, 2014, 2018, 2021; district-heating failure is the cascading risk.

hazards_alt.division: Tselinograd district (admin-2 of Akmolinskaya, surrounds Astana), code 37174

regions.hz_note_ja: River flood High and urban flood High (Akmola) describe the April snowmelt freshet: in 2024 the Zhabay river overtopped an earth dam at Atbasar on 11 April and Akmola was among the 12 flood regions, while Astana's Yesil protective dam held about 160 of its 450 million m3 capacity. Urban flooding in Astana is thaw ponding and ice jams on flat ground rather than storm runoff. Earthquake Medium at admin-1 level is a boundary effect of the global model; the Tselinograd district is Very low and USGS has no M5 event within 150 km since 1950. Wildfire High reflects steppe and pine-belt fires (Kostanay 2022, Abai 2023 nearby); extreme cold (not in ThinkHazard) is the distinctive hazard: -30 to -45 C spells and blizzards, with district-heating failure as the cascading risk.

flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: the spring 2024 floods (Atbasar dam overtopping on 11 April; Akmola among 12 affected regions; more than 120,000 evacuated nationally) and the April 2017 and 2015 Akmola/Karaganda snowmelt floods (EM-DAT 2015: 2 deaths, 12,670 affected, USD 5.3 M; 2017: 7,000 affected).

scen.10: Normal high freshet: low-lying streets of Atbasar, Yesil-district villages and Astana dacha belts flooded for days; a few hundred evacuated
scen.50: 2017-type: ice jams and snowmelt flood several Akmola towns, 5-10 thousand affected, regional roads cut for a week
scen.100: 2024-type: earth dams overtopped at Atbasar and on tributaries, 20-30 thousand evacuated in the region, Astana's protective dam under watch
scen.500: 2024 snowpack plus rapid thaw and rain: Astana's Yesil dam at capacity, left-bank suburbs and the Koyandy/Kosshy satellite towns flooded, weeks of disruption
scen.1000: Failure of the Astana (Vyacheslav) reservoir dam or the city levees: inundation of riverside districts of the capital

flood.method_ja: loss = loss_max x k. k is the shape of the WRI Aqueduct national riverine urban-damage curve for Kazakhstan (2010 baseline; USD 7069.5 M at 10 yr to 20544.6 M at 1,000 yr), so k[1000]=1. loss_max = an assumed regional share (8%) of the national 1,000-year Aqueduct damage. Depth, area, affected population and downtime scale with the same k (population and downtime with k^2.5 in the app). This is a screening model, not a hydraulic study.
assumptions_ja: Regional share 8% of the national Aqueduct damage is assumed (Astana+Akmola hold about 12% of the population and the Yesil basin was a core 2024 flood area, but Astana's dam and levees limit urban damage).
The 2024 flood is treated as roughly a 100-year event for Akmola; Tokayev called it the worst in 80 years nationally.
Dam-safety failures (Atbasar 2024) are included in the 100-year scenario; the 1,000-year scenario assumes a major reservoir failure above the capital.
Aqueduct is a 2010-baseline model without local protection.

urban_flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: spring thaw ponding on the flat left bank of Astana (snow of 1 m melting in two weeks) and summer cloudbursts; no public loss data, all values assumed.

scen.10: Meltwater pools on courtyards and underpasses for a few days each April; minor basement flooding
scen.50: Rapid thaw with frozen storm drains: 30-50 cm on main left-bank avenues for a day, traffic paralysed
scen.100: Thaw plus heavy rain: ground-floor shops and parking garages flooded in new districts, 1-2 days of disruption
scen.500: Multi-day event combined with river high water backing up the drains
scen.1000: Drainage failure across the left bank with sewage overflow

urban_flood.method_ja: Loss is a rough product of disrupted business days and affected area; not based on a public loss record.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed at USD 60 M per day for two days of capital-wide disruption.
Affected population 3% (new left-bank districts and suburbs).

quake.anchor_ja: National loss curve: GEM profile. Akmola and Astana do not appear in GEM's regional AAL list (they fall in 'Rest of Country', USD 33.9 k/yr in total), so the share is set to 0.2%, an assumption consistent with the Very low ThinkHazard level for the Tselinograd district and the absence of any catalogued earthquake within 150 km of Astana.

scen.10: No perceptible shaking; distant Tien Shan events are not felt
scen.50: Weak long-period motion in high-rises from a large distant earthquake (Kyrgyzstan/Xinjiang M7+), no damage
scen.100: Light shaking (MMI III-IV) from a rare M5 in the Kazakh Uplands; cosmetic cracks
scen.500: Unexpected moderate local event (M5.5) in the stable platform: minor damage to old brick housing
scen.1000: Hypothetical M6 intraplate event near the capital (not supported by the catalogue); limited structural damage

quake.method_ja: loss = GEM national building-loss curve for Kazakhstan (USD 13.6 M at 10 yr, 162.5 M at 50 yr, 332.3 M at 100 yr, about 1,100 M at 500 yr, about 1,700 M at 1,000 yr; residential+commercial+industrial, 2025 USD) x share. share is the region's fraction of GEM's regional AAL split. k is an assumed relative intensity used only for affected population and downtime.
assumptions_ja: Share 0.2% is an assumption; GEM groups the area into 'Rest of Country'.
Affected population 0.5% and downtime 1 day at k=1.
USGS ComCat: zero events of any magnitude within 150 km of Astana.

heat.anchor_ja: Anchor: July heat waves above 35 C in the steppe (2021 drought year; press reported record heat in the capital in July 2026 - unverified). No public loss data; values assumed.

scen.10: 3-5 days above 33 C: cooling demand, outdoor work limits
scen.50: A week above 36 C with steppe-fire smoke
scen.100: 10 days above 38 C: power and water pressure problems, crop losses in Akmola
scen.500: Two weeks of 38-40 C with drought and fires
scen.1000: Record heat dome above 42 C with regional crop failure

heat.method_ja: Loss is an assumed productivity, outage and crop cost; affected population is the share exposed to heat-health risk.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed USD 60 M.
Affected population 20%.

cold.anchor_ja: Anchor: the January 2018 Arctic cyclone (about -40 C; 223 frostbite hospital visits nationally), the 2012-13 winter (-40 to -46 C) and the 1893 record of -51.6 C in Astana; the cascading scenario is a district-heating failure during a cold spell as happened at Ekibastuz (Pavlodar Region) in November 2022 (from memory, unverified). Extra return-period block added because extreme cold is the region's distinctive hazard; values assumed.

scen.10: A week at -30 to -35 C with blizzards: schools closed, intercity roads shut, frostbite cases
scen.50: 2018-type -40 C spell for 7-10 days: hundreds of frostbite cases, localised heating-pipe bursts
scen.100: -42 C spell with a heating-plant outage in one district: thousands without heat for 2-3 days, evacuation to warming centres
scen.500: City-wide heating failure at -40 C for a week (Ekibastuz 2022 type at capital scale): mass temporary relocation
scen.1000: Record cold below -50 C with multi-day power and heating collapse

cold.method_ja: Loss assumed for a capital-scale heating failure (emergency housing, burst pipes, lost output); population and downtime scale with k^2.5.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed USD 300 M.
Affected population 50% at k=1 (district heating serves most apartments).
Return periods are expert assumptions; climate warming lowers the frequency of extreme minima but not the heating-failure risk.

history.name_ja: 2024 spring floods: Atbasar dam overtopping and Yesil high water around Astana
history.scope_ja: Akmola Region (Atbasar, Zhaksy, Yesil districts) and Astana
history.note_ja: On 11 April the Zhabay River overflowed an earth dam and Atbasar residents were evacuated; Ishimskoye and Dvurechnoye villages flooded; Astana's Yesil protective dam held about 160 of 450 million m3 and the city DES called the situation stable on 20 April. Nationally more than 117,000 evacuated by 18 April, 12 regions affected.
history.jp_ja: Astana offices were not flooded but staff with family in Akmola towns were displaced; highways to Petropavlovsk and Kostanay were cut for days.

history.name_ja: 2017 snowmelt floods in Akmola and North Kazakhstan (Atbasar)
history.scope_ja: Akmola and North Kazakhstan regions
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 2017 Kazakhstan flood total: 7,000 affected, no deaths recorded. Atbasar was flooded in April 2017 (from memory; not verified in this session).
history.jp_ja: Recurring April pattern on the Zhabay/Yesil; sites in Atbasar and Kokshetau need spring flood checks.

history.name_ja: 2015 spring floods in central and northern Kazakhstan
history.scope_ja: Karaganda, Akmola and neighbouring regions (location from memory)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 2015 Kazakhstan flood total: 2 deaths, 12,670 affected, USD 5.3 M.
history.jp_ja: Moderate, frequent events; dachas and village housing most exposed.

history.name_ja: January 2018 Arctic cold wave, about -40 C
history.scope_ja: Northern and central Kazakhstan incl. Astana
history.note_ja: Health Ministry: 223 people treated for frostbite, 73 admitted; schools closed, roads shut.
history.jp_ja: Expatriate staff unused to -40 C need vehicle survival kits and a rule not to travel by road in blizzards.

history.name_ja: January-February 2021 cold wave with frostbite deaths
history.scope_ja: Kostanay, Astana, Semey
history.note_ja: Two women died of frostbite in Kostanay Region; 14 hospitalised in Astana, 11 in Semey (press).
history.jp_ja: Cold-weather deaths are mostly people stranded outdoors; check staff commuting routes.

history.name_ja: Winter 2012-13 cold wave (-40 to -46 C)
history.scope_ja: Northern Kazakhstan
history.note_ja: Described in press as the worst cold wave on record for the region. EM-DAT 2012 lists 5,000 affected by extreme temperature.
history.jp_ja: Benchmark for a 50-year cold scenario.

history.name_ja: 2022 Kostanay Region forest fires (Auliekol), neighbouring region
history.scope_ja: Auliekol district, Kostanay Region (about 400 km west of Astana)
history.note_ja: About 43,000 ha burned, 108 houses destroyed, 1,841 evacuated, state of emergency 4 September; smoke across the northern steppe.
history.jp_ja: Smoke and road closures affect the Astana-Kostanay corridor; sites in pine-belt towns should keep fire breaks.

history.name_ja: 1997 cold wave (EM-DAT: 600,000 affected)
history.scope_ja: Northern Kazakhstan (location inferred)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 1997 Kazakhstan extreme-temperature event: 600,000 affected, no deaths recorded; also 8,000 affected by wildfire that year.
history.jp_ja: Shows the scale of population affected when heating and transport fail in the north.

flood.note_ja: Snowmelt freshet on the Yesil, Zhabay, Nura and Seleti; peak in April (2024: 28 March to 10 April GDACS alert).

urban_flood.note_ja: Thaw ponding in April, cloudbursts June-July.

cold.note_ja: January mean -14.5 C; Arctic outbreaks to -40 C and blizzards (buran) December-February.

haze.note_ja: Steppe and pine-forest fires April-September; coal-smoke smog in December-January.

water.note_ja: Summer drought on the grain belt (2021).

regions.hazard_scope_ja: ThinkHazard admin-1 level (Atyrauskaya, code 1717); the Atyrau City area division (37207) has identical levels
regions.pop_src: Atyrau Region 681,241 (2022; Atyrau city 404,129 in 2024) - Wikipedia infoboxes (third_party)
regions.desc_ja: Oil region on the north-east Caspian shore (Tengiz, Kashagan, Atyrau refinery) in the Caspian Depression, 20-28 m below sea level, flat and semi-desert. Atyrau city straddles the Zhaiyk (Ural) river at its mouth; Kulsary (about 50,000 people) lies on the Zhem (Emba). Spring snowmelt floods from upstream Russia and Aktobe (2024 Kulsary inundation) and chronic water scarcity as the Caspian and Ural fall to historic lows dominate; earthquakes are negligible and summers reach 45 C.

extreme_cold.note: Assumed Medium: January mean about -8 C, spells to -30 C with strong wind; milder than Astana.

regions.hz_note_ja: River flood High and urban flood High capture the April-May snowmelt freshet of the Zhaiyk/Ural (fed from Russia's Orenburg region, where the Orsk dam failed in April 2024) and of the Zhem/Emba, which inundated Kulsary in April 2024 (2,810 houses flooded, 33,641 people in evacuation centres at the peak); the flat, below-sea-level terrain means floodwater spreads widely and drains slowly. Coastal flood is 'No data' because the Caspian is outside the global coastal model, yet wind-driven surges of 1-2 m and the 1978-1995 sea-level rise flooded coastal oilfields (unverified); the current trend is the opposite - the sea has receded more than 50 km in the Ural delta since 2001 and reached a historic low (-29.27 m) in 2025, which underpins the water-scarcity High rating and threatens port and water intakes. Earthquake Very low: no M5 event within 150 km in USGS ComCat (largest M4.4 near Karaton in 2022). Wildfire High refers to reed-bed and steppe fires; dust storms and 45 C heat add to summer risk.

flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: the April-May 2024 floods - Kulsary on the Zhem inundated from about 5 April (2,810 houses flooded, 33,641 people in evacuation centres), then the Zhaiyk/Ural peak reached Atyrau in mid-May with 24-hour levee watches; GDACS Orange alert FL-2024-000039-KAZ. Earlier: EM-DAT 1993 flood (10 deaths, 30,000 affected, USD 36.5 M; location unverified) and the 2011 Ural floods (USD 67 M nationally).

scen.10: Zhaiyk/Zhem high water floods dacha belts and low streets of Atyrau and Kulsary for days; temporary dikes built
scen.50: 2011-type: villages along the Zhaiyk and Zhem evacuated, several thousand affected, oilfield roads cut
scen.100: 2024-type: Kulsary largely under water for weeks, 30,000+ in shelters, Atyrau levees at the limit, Tengiz logistics disrupted
scen.500: Upstream dam failures plus record snowpack: Atyrau's riverside districts flooded, refinery and port operations suspended for weeks
scen.1000: Zhaiyk levee failure in Atyrau city combined with a Caspian surge: most of the city and delta settlements inundated

flood.method_ja: loss = loss_max x k. k is the shape of the WRI Aqueduct national riverine urban-damage curve for Kazakhstan (2010 baseline; USD 7069.5 M at 10 yr to 20544.6 M at 1,000 yr), so k[1000]=1. loss_max = an assumed regional share (7%) of the national 1,000-year Aqueduct damage. Depth, area, affected population and downtime scale with the same k (population and downtime with k^2.5 in the app). This is a screening model, not a hydraulic study.
assumptions_ja: Regional share 7% of the national Aqueduct damage is assumed: the region has only 3.4% of the population, but 2024 showed it carries a disproportionate share of flood damage (Kulsary) and hosts high-value oil infrastructure.
The 2024 Kulsary flood is treated as roughly a 100-year event; losses above the 100-year level grow because of levee failure and industrial exposure.
Aqueduct is a 2010-baseline urban-damage model without local protection or oilfield assets; industrial losses could exceed the modelled value.
Affected population 10% at k=1 (Kulsary plus riverside Atyrau).

scen.100: Multi-day ponding across low districts, ground floors flooded, sewage overflow

scen.1000: City drainage failure with a Caspian surge raising the groundwater

history.name_ja: 2024 Kulsary (Zhem river) flood
history.scope_ja: Kulsary and Zhylyoi district, Atyrau Region
history.note_ja: Snowmelt from the Aktobe steppe swelled the Zhem/Emba; official updates reported 2,810 residential buildings still flooded and 33,641 people in evacuation centres; residents later protested at the district akimat over compensation. Part of the national 2024 floods (more than 120,000 evacuated).
history.jp_ja: Kulsary is the main dormitory town for Tengiz oilfield staff; rotation flights and road access were disrupted for weeks.

history.name_ja: 2024 Zhaiyk (Ural) flood peak at Atyrau
history.scope_ja: Atyrau city and Zhaiyk delta
history.note_ja: After the Orsk dam failure in Russia (5 April) the Zhaiyk crest travelled downstream; Atyrau kept a 24-hour levee vigil in mid-May while the level rose; dacha areas near Uralsk had been evacuated earlier.
history.jp_ja: Riverside offices and housing in Atyrau should plan for multi-week levee alerts rather than flash floods.

history.name_ja: 2021 drought and heat wave in western Kazakhstan
history.scope_ja: Mangystau, Atyrau, Kyzylorda, Turkistan
history.note_ja: Record 46.5 C on 7 July 2021; pasture failure and mass livestock deaths (official 1,154 cattle in Mangystau, herders' estimates far higher); more than 70,000 people affected, 84% in Mangystau.
history.jp_ja: Heat limits outdoor work at oilfields; water trucking and fodder shortages hit local communities and suppliers.

history.name_ja: Caspian Sea at a historic low (-29.27 m Kazakh sector, 2025)
history.scope_ja: North-east Caspian coast, Ural delta
history.note_ja: Kazakh Research Institute of the Caspian Sea: level fell from -26.82 m (1996) to -29.27 m (2025), -29.42 m at Kulaly in July 2026; the sea has receded over 50 km since 2001 in the Ural delta and 16,384 km2 of the north-east Caspian dried between 2000 and 2025; dredging keeps the Ural mouth and Aktau/Kuryk ports open.
history.jp_ja: Chronic trend affecting port access, cooling-water and fisheries; relevant for supply-chain routes via Caspian ports.

history.name_ja: M4.4 earthquake near Karaton (Tengiz area) - largest in the catalogue within 150 km
history.scope_ja: 35 km SW of Karaton, Zhylyoi district
history.note_ja: USGS ComCat us6000ii6e: mb 4.4, depth 10 km, 141 km from Atyrau; no M5+ event within 150 km of Atyrau since 1950.
history.jp_ja: Confirms negligible seismic risk; no seismic retrofit needed beyond code.

history.name_ja: 1993 spring flood (EM-DAT: 10 deaths, 30,000 affected, USD 36.5 M)
history.scope_ja: Western Kazakhstan (Ural basin; location inferred, unverified)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 1993 Kazakhstan flood total; the largest pre-2008 flood loss in the series. Attribution to the Ural basin is an inference.
history.jp_ja: Benchmark for a 50-year regional flood.

history.name_ja: 2011 Ural (Zhaiyk) basin floods (EM-DAT: 2 deaths, 16,000 affected, USD 67 M)
history.scope_ja: West Kazakhstan and Atyrau regions (location from memory)
history.note_ja: EM-DAT 2011 Kazakhstan flood total; the April 2011 Ural flood around Uralsk is remembered as the previous major event before 2024 (unverified).

history.name_ja: Caspian sea-level rise 1978-1995 (about +2.5 m) flooding coastal lowlands and oilfields

regions.hazard_scope_ja: ThinkHazard admin-1 level (Yujno-kazachstanskaya = former South Kazakhstan Region, code 1728, which includes Shymkent); the Shymkent City area division (37319) is given in hazards_alt
regions.pop_src: Shymkent 1,274,296 (1 Jun 2025, Wikipedia infobox) + Turkistan Region about 2.1 M (assumed from Bureau of National Statistics 2024 figures; the Wikipedia infobox value 2,685,009 is a 2013 pre-split figure that includes Shymkent) - third_party / assumed
regions.desc_ja: Kazakhstan's third city (city of republican significance since 2018) and the densely populated irrigated south along the Syr Darya, Arys, Keles and Badam rivers, bordering Uzbekistan 100 km from Tashkent. The Ugam-Karatau foothills of the western Tien Shan bring the country's highest earthquake loss (GEM AAL USD 6.9 M/yr for the region) and spring mudflows on loess soils; the Syr Darya lowlands (Maktaaral) were flooded by the 2020 Sardoba dam failure in Uzbekistan. Summers reach 46 C and water allocation on the Syr Darya is contested.

extreme_cold.note: Assumed Low: mild winters (January mean about -2 C), occasional -20 C spells and black ice.

hazards_alt.division: Shymkent City area (admin-2 under Yujno-kazachstanskaya), code 37319

regions.hz_note_ja: At region level river flood, urban flood, earthquake, landslide, water scarcity and wildfire are all High, while the Shymkent city division is Low for floods and Medium for earthquake: the floods belong to the Syr Darya/Arys lowlands (Sardoba 2020: 31,606 evacuated in Maktaaral; February 2023 floods near Turkistan and Kentau; EM-DAT 2008 flood USD 130 M) and to foothill rivers, and the mudflow (landslide) rating to the Ugam, Karatau and Sayram ranges where spring rain on loess produces debris flows. Earthquake High reflects the western Tien Shan fault systems: 1937 Zhabagly Mw 6.4 (120 km from Shymkent), 1966 Tashkent (about 120 km), 1987 Gazalkent Mw 5.2 (73 km), 1992 Suusamyr Mw 7.3 felt; GEM ranks South Kazakhstan first for seismic loss. Extreme heat Medium understates 2021's 46.5 C record; water scarcity High is about Syr Darya allocation and the Aral basin.

flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: the 1 May 2020 Sardoba reservoir failure in Uzbekistan that flooded Maktaaral district (31,606 evacuated from 14 settlements, 5 villages with 6,127 people fully flooded; EM-DAT 2020: 33,000 affected in Kazakhstan), the March 2008 South Kazakhstan floods (EM-DAT USD 130 M, 13,000 affected) and the February 2023 rain-on-snow floods around Turkistan and Kentau (200+ evacuated).

scen.10: February-April rain-on-snow floods in Baidibek, Ordabasy, Sauran and Kentau districts: tens of houses flooded, a few hundred evacuated, bridges washed out
scen.50: 2008-type: Arys and Badam floods and ice jams, 10-15 thousand affected across the region, Shymkent suburbs waterlogged
scen.100: 2020 Sardoba-type trans-boundary dam failure or Shardara emergency release: 30,000+ evacuated from the Syr Darya lowlands, cotton and farm losses
scen.500: Shardara reservoir failure or extreme Syr Darya flood: Maktaaral and Zhetysai under water for weeks, cross-border rail and roads cut
scen.1000: Combined Syr Darya and foothill-river floods with mudflows; southern districts of Shymkent and the Turkistan plain inundated

flood.method_ja: loss = loss_max x k. k is the shape of the WRI Aqueduct national riverine urban-damage curve for Kazakhstan (2010 baseline; USD 7069.5 M at 10 yr to 20544.6 M at 1,000 yr), so k[1000]=1. loss_max = an assumed regional share (10%) of the national 1,000-year Aqueduct damage. Depth, area, affected population and downtime scale with the same k (population and downtime with k^2.5 in the app). This is a screening model, not a hydraulic study.
assumptions_ja: Regional share 10% of the national Aqueduct damage is assumed: the region holds about 16% of the population, with large irrigated lowlands but low asset values.
The 2020 Sardoba flood is treated as roughly a 100-year event because it depends on dam failure upstream in Uzbekistan.
Aqueduct is a 2010-baseline urban-damage model without reservoir operations (Shardara, Koksaray).
Affected population 5% at k=1 (Syr Darya lowland districts).

urban_flood.anchor_ja: Anchor: the March 2024 downpours that flooded streets and courtyards in Shymkent and Turkistan Region districts (press) and recurring spring storms on the Badam and Koshkar-Ata channels; no public loss data, values assumed.

scen.10: Spring downpour: 20-40 cm on low streets and the old-town courtyards for hours
scen.50: 2024-type: streets and yards across several districts flooded, markets closed for a day
scen.100: Storm plus Badam river overflow: 0.5-0.7 m in low districts, 1-2 days of disruption
scen.500: Multi-day rain on saturated loess with mud on roads and drainage collapse
scen.1000: City-wide drainage failure combined with foothill mudflows

urban_flood.method_ja: Loss is a rough product of disrupted business days and affected area; not based on a public loss record.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed USD 50 M per day for two days.
Affected population 3% at k=1.

quake.anchor_ja: National loss curve: GEM profile. GEM's regional split gives South Kazakhstan Region (incl. Shymkent) USD 6.9 M/yr of the national 16.3 M/yr, i.e. 42%, the largest share of any region; this share is applied to the national curve.

scen.10: M5 within 150 km (2011 Taraz M5.0 type): felt widely, people leave buildings, no damage
scen.50: 1987 Gazalkent-type Mw 5.2 at 73 km or a local M5.5: cracks in adobe and old brick houses in villages
scen.100: 1937 Zhabagly-type Mw 6.4 in the Talas Alatau: damage to unreinforced housing in Tulkibas and Sayram districts, some collapses
scen.500: M6.5-7 on the Karatau or Ugam faults close to Shymkent: widespread collapse of adobe and old masonry, thousands of casualties, weeks without services
scen.1000: M7+ western Tien Shan rupture (Suusamyr 1992 scale) near the city: regional disaster with Tashkent also hit

quake.method_ja: loss = GEM national building-loss curve for Kazakhstan (USD 13.6 M at 10 yr, 162.5 M at 50 yr, 332.3 M at 100 yr, about 1,100 M at 500 yr, about 1,700 M at 1,000 yr; residential+commercial+industrial, 2025 USD) x share. share is the region's fraction of GEM's regional AAL split. k is an assumed relative intensity used only for affected population and downtime.
assumptions_ja: Share 42% from GEM's loss-by-region chart (region boundaries pre-2018, including Shymkent).
Affected population 25% at k=1 (adobe and old masonry housing dominate rural districts).
Downtime up to 45 days.

scen.10: Mudflow blocks a mountain road and damages a few houses in a foothill village
scen.50: Several villages hit, dozens of houses destroyed, the Shymkent-Tashkent or Tulkibas roads cut for days
scen.100: Rain-on-snow plus earthquake-weakened slopes: hundreds of houses damaged, casualties
scen.500: Large landslide dams a foothill river and bursts, flooding a district town
scen.1000: Earthquake-triggered landslides across the foothills (Khait 1949 type at smaller scale)

landslide.method_ja: Loss scaled from an assumed USD 100 M foothill event; return periods are expert assumptions.
assumptions_ja: Loss at k=1 assumed USD 100 M.
