history.name_ja: 1923 earthquake south of Istaravshan, ISC-GEM Mw 6.47
history.scope_ja: Turkestan range, 29 km S of Istaravshan, 87 km from Khujand
history.note_ja: Largest catalogued event within 150 km of Khujand (USGS iscgem911786, 20 km deep); casualties not found in reachable sources.

history.name_ja: 1985 Kayrakkum (Qayroqqum) earthquake, Mw 5.8, MMI IX
history.scope_ja: Kayrakkum/Guliston and Ghafurov, 15-25 km E of Khujand
history.note_ja: 29 dead, 80+ injured, 8,000 homeless; 90% of multi-storey brick buildings in Kayrakkum destroyed, carpet factory collapse, reservoir embankments damaged, MMI VII in Khujand (Leninabad); USD 200 M (1985). USGS usp0002ks3, 17 km from Khujand.
history.jp_ja: The reference event for industrial sites in the Khujand-Ghafurov-Kayrakkum belt (factory collapse on the evening shift).

history.name_ja: July 1999 floods and landslides: Asht and Ayni (Sughd), Jirgatal
history.scope_ja: Asht (18 dead, 50 missing, 167 houses destroyed, 209 damaged), Ayni; also DRS districts
history.note_ja: Torrential rain 6-12 July 1999; EM-DAT 1999 flood total 27 deaths, USD 6.2 M; hundreds of houses, roads, bridges and canals destroyed in northern and central Tajikistan.

history.name_ja: 2007 Asht mudflow (Oshoba jamoat resort area): 12 dead
history.scope_ja: Olma and Chimor villages, Oshoba jamoat, Asht district
history.note_ja: Mudflow at 14:00 local time ripped through a resort area killing 12 (UNCT); the same day an M5.2-5.5 earthquake struck Rasht (3 dead).

history.name_ja: 2008 cold wave/energy crisis and May 2008 Sughd rains
history.scope_ja: Nationwide; Sughd on 1-3 hours of electricity per day, Dushanbe-Khujand road closed by avalanches and mudflows in March
history.note_ja: Coldest winter in 44 years (EM-DAT: 2,000,000 affected, USD 840 M nationally); preliminary damage from heavy rains in Sughd in May 2008 put at 63 M somoni (Asia-Plus).
history.jp_ja: Northern Tajikistan depends on electricity imports and the Dushanbe road in winter; plan for weeks of rationing.

history.name_ja: 2011 Fergana Valley earthquake, Mw 6.2 (Batken, Kyrgyzstan): 14 dead in Kyrgyzstan/Uzbekistan, felt across Sughd
history.scope_ja: Epicentre 16 km NNE of Aydarken (Kyrgyzstan), 70 km E of Isfara; MMI VIII
history.note_ja: USGS M6.1-6.2 at 20 km depth; Wikipedia list gives 14 dead and 86 injured (in Fergana, Uzbekistan and Batken, Kyrgyzstan); damage in Isfara/Konibodom not quantified.

history.name_ja: May 2016 Panjakent and Ayni mudflows
history.scope_ja: Panjakent (147 households on 9 May), Ayni; also Rudaki and Rasht
history.note_ja: Mudflows 9-12 May 2016 killed at least four in Sughd; national toll 6 by 3 June (REACT).

history.name_ja: June 2017 mudflows: Amondara (Panjakent) 16 households, Ayni 1 dead, Shahriston houses damaged
history.scope_ja: Panjakent, Ayni and Shahriston districts
history.note_ja: Amondara mudflow on 26 June 2017 damaged 16 households (6 destroyed); one killed and one injured in Ayni (Asia-Plus).

history.name_ja: July 2021 Panjakent mudslides (Dashti Kozi, Kishtudak): 10-12 dead incl. four children
history.scope_ja: Panjakent district, Zeravshan valley; mudflows in four Sughd districts on 19 July
history.note_ja: Night-time mudslides after heavy rain; CoES/RFE/RL 10 dead and 2 missing, later reports 12; same week 16 died in mudslides in Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

history.name_ja: 2023 Kuhistoni Mastchoh earthquake, Mw 5.8: 318 houses damaged
history.scope_ja: Paldorak, Langar jamoat, Kuhistoni Mastchoh district (upper Zeravshan); felt at 3-4 in Dushanbe
history.note_ja: USGS us7000jm0r (22 Mar 20:07 UTC, 12 km deep; 102 km from Khujand); 3 injured; 318 houses from the 1970s-80s on hillsides damaged (Governmental Commission, 28 Mar 2023).

history.name_ja: June 2024 mudflows in Sughd (Shahriston, Kuhistoni Mastchoh) after Tajikhydromet warning; 25 mudflow deaths nationally in 2024
history.scope_ja: Sarvakht (Shahriston) 11 June, Oburdon (Kuhistoni Mastchoh) 12 June; rockfalls in GBAO
history.note_ja: Torrential rain 11-13 June 2024 damaged plots and roads; Hydromet had warned of flooding and landslides in Sughd for 13-14 June; nationwide 25 mudflow deaths in 2024 (Times of Central Asia citing CoES). GDACS flood alerts 11-13 Jun 2024.
history.src_name: Asia-Plus / Times of Central Asia (search snippets) / GDACS

history.name_ja: July 2026 Ayni flash floods and mudflows (Darg and Kazdon villages): 672 households affected
history.scope_ja: Shamtuch jamoat, Ayni district, Zeravshan valley
history.note_ja: Intense rain at about 15:40 on 11 July 2026; 672 households affected, 67 houses damaged (3 destroyed), water, irrigation, power and roads damaged (IFRC DREF MDRTJ038). A May 2026 Isfara mudflow destroyed house walls.
history.jp_ja: The Ayni section of the Dushanbe-Khujand road is the single supply route for northern sites; allow for multi-day closures.

flood.note_ja: Spring rain floods Apr-Jun in the Zeravshan/Isfara/Asht valleys; Syr Darya snowmelt peak Jun-Jul; July cloudbursts (1999, 2021, 2026)

landslide.note_ja: Avalanches/rockfalls on the Anzob-Ayni road Feb-Mar; mudflows Apr-Jul

cold.note_ja: January cold (record -22.8 C) with electricity rationing

haze.note_ja: Dust storms Jun-Oct; winter smog in the Khujand basin

water.note_ja: Irrigation season; dependence on Toktogul releases
